draft.title: Energy profile diagrams
card: An energy profile diagram plots the energy of the chemicals (vertical axis) against the progress of the reaction (horizontal axis). The reactants are the level at the start and the products are the level at the end.
the minimum energy needed to start the reaction. It is the height from the reactants' level up to the top of the peak.
the energy change of the reaction. It is the products' level minus the reactants' level, so it is measured from the reactants to the products, not to the peak.
If the products sit lower than the reactants, ΔH is negative. If the products sit higher, ΔH is positive.
draft.remember: Activation energy is reactants up to the peak. ΔH is reactants to products.

a.q: On an energy profile diagram, what does the height from the reactants' level to the top of the peak show?
a.why: The peak is the energy barrier the reactants must climb to react, so that height is the activation energy. It is not ΔH, because ΔH is measured from the reactants to the products and not to the peak.
a.clue: Think about the energy needed to get the reaction started.

b.q: In a diagram for a reaction, the reactants are at 200 kJ, the peak is at 350 kJ and the products are at 120 kJ. What are the activation energy and ΔH?
b.why: Activation energy is the peak minus the reactants: 350 - 200 = 150 kJ. ΔH is the products minus the reactants: 120 - 200 = -80 kJ, because the products sit lower. Using 230 kJ measures from the products to the peak, which is not the activation energy.
b.clue: Both values start from the reactants' level.
